facts.title: What Zurich wants to know, and what it costs you

items.title: You have to declare it
items.body: Anyone who files a tax return in Zurich declares income and assets worldwide. That includes an apartment in Valencia, Berlin or Kyiv, even if nobody lives there.

items.title: Switzerland does not tax it
items.body: Swiss law taxes real estate only in the country where it stands, and Switzerland's tax treaties say the same. Zurich removes the apartment from your taxable wealth and income.

items.title: It only moves your tax rate
items.body: The value and a notional rent are used to set your rate. For a typical apartment the effect is small. Leaving the apartment out is what gets expensive: back taxes, interest and a fine.

items.title: Describe your apartment
items.body: Country, city, size, what you paid or what it is worth, and how it is used today: kept for yourself, lived in by family, rented out, or not usable.

items.title: Get the Zurich values
items.body: Tax value at 70% of the price. Notional rent at 4.25% for apartments or 3.5% for houses. The 20% flat deduction for maintenance. All converted to francs.

items.title: Copy the numbers into your tax return
items.body: The result mirrors the Zurich property form line by line, with a ready German note for the remarks field. Type it into ZHprivateTax or the paper form.

items.q: Do I pay Swiss tax on my apartment abroad?
items.a: No. Swiss law taxes real estate only in the country where it stands, and Switzerland's tax treaties say the same. Zurich still wants to see the apartment because your total wealth and income decide which tax rate applies to the part that is taxable in Switzerland. Tax people call this satzbestimmend, meaning it counts for the rate only.

items.q: The other country already taxes the apartment. Is that not double taxation?
items.a: No. The other country taxes the property and any rent from it. Switzerland does not tax them again, it only uses them to set the rate on your Swiss income and wealth. Whatever you owe abroad, for example German tax on rent (Anlage V) or the Spanish non-resident tax (Modelo 210), is a separate filing in that country.

{price} per apartment for your first declaration. In the following years it costs less, because your apartment is already set up. A tax adviser usually charges several hundred francs for the same work, every year.

items.q: My tax is deducted from my salary. Do I file a tax return at all?
items.a: People taxed at source (Quellensteuer), for example with a B permit or protection status S, usually do not file. You must file if you have other income of CHF 3'000 or more per year, taxable wealth of CHF 80'000 or more (CHF 160'000 for married couples), or a gross salary of CHF 120'000 or more. With status S you also become fully taxable once you have lived in Switzerland for more than two years without interruption and your life is centred here. And if your municipality sent you a tax return, you have to complete it in any case. If you are unsure, ask your Gemeindesteueramt.

items.q: How do I value the apartment?
items.a: Zurich practice for property abroad is 70% of the purchase price, converted to francs. If there was no purchase price, for example because the apartment was inherited or given to you, use a realistic estimate of what it would sell for and take 70% of that. Keep whatever supports your number: the purchase contract, a land register extract, or comparable listings.

items.q: My apartment is damaged or cannot be used. What now?
items.a: You still list it, because you still own it. Use a value that reflects reality, and do not declare any notional rent if the apartment really cannot be used, for example after war damage or a fire, or because it is in an area you cannot reach. The tool writes a short German explanation for the remarks field. Keep photos, official reports or news coverage in case the tax office asks.

items.q: My parents live in the apartment for free. Is that rental income?
items.a: It is not rent, but Zurich treats an apartment used by you or your relatives free of charge as used by yourself. That means a notional rent (Eigenmietwert) of 4.25% of the tax value applies. It affects your rate only.

items.q: What is Eigenmietwert, and was it not abolished?
items.a: It is a notional income: what you could earn if you rented out a home you keep for yourself. Swiss voters decided on 28 September 2025 to abolish it, and the Federal Council set 1 January 2029 as the start date. Up to and including tax year 2028 it still has to be declared.

items.q: I did not declare the apartment in earlier years. What should I do?
items.a: Once in your life you can correct this without a fine through a voluntary disclosure (straflose Selbstanzeige), as long as the tax office has not found out on its own. You pay the missing tax for up to ten years plus interest, which for a foreign apartment is usually a small amount. Contact the cantonal tax office or an adviser before you file, and do not simply start listing the apartment without explanation.

items.q: What about my bank accounts abroad?
items.a: Once you are fully taxable in Switzerland, foreign accounts belong in the securities and accounts list (Wertschriftenverzeichnis) with the balance on 31 December and the interest earned. This tool only covers real estate.

items.q: Does this affect my social assistance?
items.a: Social assistance, asylum support and supplementary benefits follow their own rules and are handled by a different office. This tool only covers the tax return. Tell your caseworker about the property truthfully and ask how it is treated in your municipality.
In your browser and nowhere else. Nothing you type is sent to a server, there is no account and no tracking. You can delete everything with one click.

guide.title: Filling in the Zurich form, step by step
guide.lead: The canton's online tax return is called ZHprivateTax. The paper form has the same fields. Here is where your apartment goes.

steps.title: Open the Liegenschaftenverzeichnis
steps.body: This is the list of real estate. Since tax year 2024 all properties are declared only here, including those in other cantons and abroad.

steps.title: Add the apartment
steps.body: Enter city and street in Latin letters. Under Kanton / Land choose the country. As type choose Stockwerkeigentum for an apartment or Einfamilienhaus for a house, and enter the area in m².

steps.title: Enter the income
steps.body: In the field Eigenmietwert / Mietzinseinnahmen enter the notional rent from your Dix.Tax sheet, or the rent you received if the apartment is rented out.

steps.title: Choose the flat deduction
steps.body: For Unterhalts- und Verwaltungskosten choose Pauschalabzug. It is 20% and needs no receipts. Actual costs are only worth it if they were higher, and then you need a detailed list.

steps.title: Enter the tax value
steps.body: In the field Verkehrswert enter the tax value from your sheet. The program carries the totals to line 6 (net income from property) and line 31.1 (property) of the main form.

steps.title: Add the German note
steps.body: Paste the note from your sheet into the remarks (Bemerkungen). It explains how you valued the apartment and asks the tax office to allocate it abroad. The office does the allocation itself.

steps.title: Submit and keep your documents
steps.body: The deadline in Zurich is 31 March. You can extend it online, free of charge, until 30 November. You do not need to send documents about the apartment, but keep them in case the office asks.

docs: Purchase contract, or the inheritance or gift document
Land register extract from the country where the property stands
Rental contract and proof of rent received, if rented
Photos, damage reports or official confirmations, if the property cannot be used
The exchange rate you used and where it came from

glossary.liegenschaftenverzeichnis: List of real estate. The form where every property is declared.
glossary.eigenmietwert: Notional rent. Income you are deemed to have from a home you keep for your own use.
glossary.steuerwert: Tax value. The value of the property for wealth tax, in Zurich also called Verkehrswert on the form.
glossary.pauschalabzug: Flat deduction. A fixed percentage you may deduct without receipts.
glossary.satzbestimmend: Counts for the rate only. The item is not taxed itself but raises the rate on everything else.
glossary.steuerausscheidung: Tax allocation. The tax office separates what is taxable in Zurich from what belongs to another country.
glossary.quellensteuer: Tax at source. Tax that the employer deducts directly from the salary.
glossary.schutzstatus: Protection status S. The residence status for people who fled the war in Ukraine.
glossary.gemeindesteueramt: Municipal tax office. Your first contact for forms, deadlines and questions.
glossary.fristerstreckung: Deadline extension. More time to file, requested online.
glossary.bemerkungen: Remarks. Free text field for explanations to the tax office.
glossary.selbstanzeige: Voluntary disclosure. Reporting earlier omissions yourself, once in a lifetime without a fine.
